description: Experiment E, retrieval modes (Phase 14 ruling 31; Phase 15 rulings 1, 6, 11 and 12, work order 4 A1 and A2, repair-02). The first 10 benchmark questions (experiments/benchmark/benchmark-questions-v1.csv, file order) are answered by the local runtime (rag BenchmarkCli, live mode: Bedrock Haiku for planning and synthesis, Titan for embeddings) under three retrieval modes, fused (the default, today's behaviour), graph-only and vector-only, sequentially, one sbt process at a time, --per-minute 8. A check step first answers 2 questions in fused mode and stops the run (exit 3, outputs kept) unless the plan sources include MODEL and the output has no FALLBACK_RULES, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED or Exception; fused then resumes those 2 with --max 8 (BenchmarkCli's --max limits the new pending questions), and graph-only and vector-only run with --max 10, so every mode answers exactly the first 10 questions (ruling 12(a)). The graph and items are the served data (run-1d6a86491812ff94887270c1ab885e69); the vector side is the file-backed export of the live vectors (scratch/stores-live/s3vectors) searched by the local exact FileVectorStore, not the S3 Vectors service (ruling 31; modules/rag/RUNTIME.md section 24). Each question's ranked retrieved list (post-budget bundle) is written per mode; no score against labels is computed during the run. Relevance labels and answer ratings are the human's only (ruling 1): experiments/analysis/e-label-sheets.py makes blind sheets afterwards, and experiments/analysis/summarize-exp-e.py computes recall at 5 and 10 and MRR only from the human's files. Run by the human through scripts/run-experiment.sh at a clean, committed HEAD after a passing check.sh (so rag is compiled), never alongside another Haiku run or another sbt process. No deployed resource is touched: nothing runs in AWS except the Bedrock invocations.

limits.maxMinutesReason: Worst-case sum with every wait at its bound, plus at least 10 minutes of margin. 4 sbt invocations (check, fused, graph-only, vector-only) x 300 s of start-up (sbt start and project load, a rag compile if one is still needed, graph load about 34 s and item index about 19 s in the Phase 10 live runs, whose whole 2-question invocation took 79 to 88 s) = 1,200 s; plus 30 questions (check --max 2, fused --max 8 more, graph-only --max 10, vector-only --max 10; ruling 12(a)) x 210 s (runtime.question.deadline-ms 180 s plus one model attempt overrunning it by runtime.llm.timeout-ms 30 s; RUNTIME.md section 23) = 6,300 s; total 7,500 s = 125 min, 10 min under 135. run-experiment.sh then sends TERM, and the harness sends TERM to sbt's process group (runner and JVM), KILL after 20 s if any member is left (inside run-experiment.sh's 30 s), and keeps harness.json.
limits.plannedBreakdown: 4 invocations x about 90 s start-up; 30 questions at about 10 to 30 s each (Phase 10 live: p50 about 15 s, max 46 s); at most 8 Haiku requests per minute, about 2 per question, so at least about 8 minutes of throttle floor
limits.questionsTotal: 10 questions x 3 modes = 30 questions (the check's 2 fused questions are among fused's 10; fused resumes them with --max 8; graph-only and vector-only --max 10; every mode answers the same first 10 question IDs)
limits.checkStopRule: continue only when the check's sbt exits 0, its 'plan sources:' line includes MODEL, and neither that line nor the check's stdout and stderr contain FALLBACK_RULES, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED or Exception; otherwise exit 3 with every output kept
limits.failingModeRule: a mode that exits non-zero is recorded in harness.json (<stamp>/raw/harness.json) and the next mode still runs; the harness then exits 1. BenchmarkCli itself stops a mode at its first failed question (no result recorded), so a rerun of the same command resumes.
limits.perMinuteNote: Haiku requests per minute (--per-minute 8; runtime.llm.requests-per-minute ruling 11 bound 1 to 8, quota 10); every attempt and retry passes the throttle. Titan is held to runtime.embedding.requests-per-minute 50.
limits.otherSbtProcessRule: the harness refuses to start (exit 3) when another sbt or runMain process is running
limits.runtime: local runtime (rag BenchmarkCli, -J-Xmx6g) on this machine against live Bedrock in us-east-2; no deployed service, no Neptune, DynamoDB or S3 Vectors call
limits.vectors: file-backed export of the live vectors under scratch/stores-live/s3vectors, searched by the local exact FileVectorStore, not the S3 Vectors service (Phase 14 ruling 31); its nearest-neighbour ranking may differ from the service's approximate search
limits.haikuModel: us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 (the configured planner and synthesis model; recorded in every audit's modelIds)
limits.haikuCallsExpected: about 2 per question (planning and synthesis; 1 when the answer abstains before synthesis), about 60 in total
limits.haikuRequestsMax: 240: 30 questions x 2 calls x max-attempts-per-call 2 x at most 2 Bedrock requests per attempt (Benchmark.MaxRequestsPerAttempt)
limits.embeddingCallsMax: 20: at most one per question (runtime embedding-budget check); graph-only makes none
limits.exitCodes: 0 every mode exited 0; 1 a mode failed; 2 usage; 3 precondition (no experiment directory or profile, another sbt process) or the check stopped; 143 terminated at maxMinutes
limits.awsCallsByHarness: none directly; the only AWS calls are BenchmarkCli's Bedrock InvokeModel requests (Haiku and Titan) with AWS_PROFILE from run-experiment.sh (and run-experiment.sh's own sts get-caller-identity)
limits.budgetNote: upper bound from the token ceilings: 30 questions x (40,000 input tokens at 1 USD per million + 9,600 output tokens at 5 USD per million, the Haiku 4.5 list price assumed) = 2.64 USD; Titan embeddings at most 20 short inputs, under 0.01 USD. Expected about 0.3 USD (Phase 10 live: about 5,800 input and 500 output tokens per question).

expectedFinding: Stated before the run and reported either way (Phase 15 ruling 6): vector-only answers are expected to abstain with NO_VERIFIED_CLAIM, because the verifier requires graph evidence for every material claim and vector-only bundles hold semantic items only (RUNTIME.md section 24). Graph-only answers are expected to keep the verified claims of fused answers but to lose the semantic context items. Recall at K and MRR are not expected values: they exist only after the human labels the pooled items.

context.vectorStore: scratch/stores-live/s3vectors (file-backed export of the live vectors, ruling 31)
context.questions: experiments/benchmark/benchmark-questions-v1.csv; BenchmarkCli answers pending questions in file order, so --max 10 is the first 10 rows
context.retrievalModesDoc: modules/rag/RUNTIME.md section 24 (Phase 15 work order 1); benchmark result rag-benchmark-result-v3 and summary rag-benchmark-summary-v3
context.outputLayout: run-experiment.sh sets SCHOLARCHAIN_EXPERIMENT_DIR to <results>/<stamp>/raw, and the harness writes directly under $SCHOLARCHAIN_EXPERIMENT_DIR (ruling 12(b), as D and F do), so the files are <stamp>/raw/harness.json and <stamp>/raw/<mode>/
context.rawOutputs: relative to <stamp>/: raw/harness.json (exp-e-harness-v1: start and end, modes, n, the check decision, and per invocation the command, exit code, times and benchmark run IDs); raw/fused/check-stdout.txt and check-stderr.txt; raw/<mode>/modes-stdout.txt and modes-stderr.txt; raw/<mode>/s3/reports/rag-benchmark/snapshot=2026-10-03/run=<benchmark run>/questions/<id>.json, summary-<nnn>.json and retrieval/<id>-<mode>.csv; raw/<mode>/s3/logs/rag-runtime/... (audits), raw/<mode>/s3/reports/rag-runtime/... (answers), raw/<mode>/s3/runs/... (manifests), raw/<mode>/dynamodb/... (QuerySession and EvidenceBundle records)
context.analysis: after the run, read-only: experiments/analysis/summarize-exp-e.py --raw <stamp>/raw --out <dir>; experiments/analysis/e-label-sheets.py --raw <stamp>/raw --out scratch/e-labelling (never under labels/); the human saves labels/relevance-e-v1.csv and the ratings, then summarize-exp-e.py --relevance --ratings --keys
context.limitations: the ranked list is the post-budget bundle, so recall at K is capped at the bundle size (Phase 15 ruling 6, m5); the vector search is local exact search over the export, not S3 Vectors; 10 questions per mode; live model output is not deterministic (temperature 0, but not guaranteed identical)
